recipes.name: Easy Baked Beans
ingredients_raw: 2 (16 ounce) cans baked beans with pork

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a casserole dish with cooking spray.
Mix together baked beans with pork, molasses, onions, brown sugar, ketchup, and mustard together in a large bowl.
Transfer mixture to the prepared dish and top with chopped bacon.
Cover and bake in the preheated oven until thickened, about 3 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Baked Beans
raw_recipe.description: These easy baked beans are made with canned beans, molasses, brown sugar, and onion baked in the oven until thick and flavorful for a simple meal.

review.reviewBody: This is so similar to baked beans that my mother-in-law used to make. I think the ingredients are the same but the way she made them was different. She cooked the bacon first and added that crumbled up to the beans instead of on top. Then she'd cook the onions in the bacon fat until they were clear. Then add the cooked onions and everything else to the beans and cook for a much shorter time in the oven. An hour or maybe less. That's how I've been making them and they're fantastic! Excellent, easy, fast recipe for baked beans: the way they were meant to be. Thanks for this recipe!

This is a very nice recipe. I followed the ingredients to the letter; however I sped up the process. I browned the bacon and sauted the onions on the stove top - added the rest and heated through. Once heated through I transferred to a crockpot to finish cooking on low 2-3 hours.

I LOVED THESE BEANS, and after reading some of the reviews there were some hints that I really liked. I wanted to serve about 10- 15 ppl. I used two large cans of the Bush's original and one of the bold and spicy. I cooked about 4- 5 pieces of bacon that I cut into small pieces before cooking. I then sauté'd the onions in the bacon grease until translucent to lightly browned. Mix together the beans, mustard, Ketchup, molasses, SKIP the brown sugar unless you like the beans even more on the sweet sweet side. MIX IN the bacon and onions. I used at least a half of large onion, 2tbs mustard and 1/4 cup ketchup. I then placed in oven cover and bake for three hours. LOVELY smell in the house, and the taste... MMMMM fabulous!!! Tastes like you cooked them completely from scratch!!

It turned out excellent! I did follow the advice to cook the bacon first and then saute the onions in the bacon fat before putting everything in the oven. 
 I also accidentally used two 28 ounce cans of baked beans the first time I made it, and the sweetness was perfect, so I never decreased the amount of baked beans the subsequent times I made the recipe because I thought it may be a little bit too sweet.

Made this for a work pot luck and they were a huge hit. I used Cambell's pork and beans as a base and altered the recipe slightly by frying the bacon first and crumbling into the bean mixture before "baking". I sauteed the onions in the bacon grease and dumped the onions along with the bacon grease into the bean mixture. I cooked in a crock pot on low for 3 hours - perfect!!!

My mother’s recipes! Love! But only add one tablespoon brown sugar tops! Also try a different flavor. Substitute maple syrup for molasses and omit sugar. I cook in an open crockpot for a thicker bean texture

I thought it was delicious! Best recipe I have used for doctored up beans. I did double the recipe and added more bacon just because but the sugar and molasses were good amounts. I put it in the crock pot and let them thicken up all day so I didn't have to heat up my house. These were much better than any Bush's beans I have tried!

2.25.20 O-M-G please do NOT plan on baking these beans for anywhere close to 3 hours or you will have a dish full of totally dried beans and burnt bacon. I checked at 1 hour, not quite done, added another 20 minutes, and yep, that did it.. They will firm up a bit as they sit. The bacon was browned and had added its good flavor to the beans, and the consistency was spot on right for us, just about perfect for baked beans. Initially, I was a little confused by the listing for the canned beans. It says ”baked beans with pork”? I thought would that be a can of beans Bush’s® baked beans, but then, they’re good-to-go right out of the can, no seasoning required. At any rate, I used 2 cans of pork and beans, and I think that was the submitter’s intent. For personal taste, I did cut the molasses and brown sugar in half. Indeed, they are very simple to make, and they are very tasty, as well. Good baked beans, just watch your time.

Made exactly as the recipe calls for, these were a huge hit at our memorial day party! I made more and this time reduced the raw bacon being put in the casserole prior to baking, I cooked until crispy the remaining amount after chopping it as well and that went over even better. So happy to have found something so simple and so tasty! Oh, and Yummi, if you are planning on feeding that many, I would definitely double or triple the recipe. Depends on whether you have hungry adults or small children included in your group. I quadrupled the recipe for the next party of 11 and it was gone in no time.

This is exactly how I make mine. I buy the most inexpensive cans of pork and beans and add all the rest. I usually taste it as I go along to make sure it isn't overly sweet. I also "bake" it in the microwave which cuts the time in half. It cooks up nice and thick the way old fashion beans cook when they are baked in the oven for hours.

This recipe is a keeper. I followed the advise of some of the others who had made it and used half the brown sugar and molasses. I cooked the bacon and onion first as I used my slow cooker. There were none left!

Love these baked beans. Growing up, my aunt used to make the best baked beans but I never got the recipe from her. So I’ve been on the hunt for the perfect baked beans and here it is I use pork and beans, not baked beans that the recipe calls for and everyone who has tried them, loves them. Also, I never bake for 3 hours. That seems like an excessively long cook time.
This baked bean recipe is delicious and cannot even justify making them from scratch anymore👍👍👍👍👍
I prepared this dish exactly as written. They were delicious and a big hit with the family. I’m making them again today and excited since they enjoyed them last time.

I pretty much followed the recipe. Left out the brown sugar because half of the cans were already brown sugar baked beans, sautéed minced garlic with the onions after cooking the bacon. Add the catsup, mustard and molasses. Declicious!

I usually never like what I cook, but these baked beans were perfect! Better than any BBQ place. I did add about 8 oz of beans because I didn’t think the recipe was enough. Glad I did because no beans were left in the dish!
I get more raves on this recipe. Like Mom used to make growing up.
I made for a 4th of July get together. It was easy and delicious. I will make again.

I made a huge pot of these beans for a potluck outdoor BBQ, and they were gone before anything else on the table. They tasted like I had soaked navy beans and slaved over a complicated recipe for hours. I preferred less sugar so I cut the brown sugar in half - still had nice homemade flavour but not so sweet!
easy to understand and make family loves them thank you
